issues.legal_issue: A complaint under the special procedure for a witness’s intentional false evidence or fabrication of evidence cannot be made after final disposition when the court did not record the required finding at that time.
material_facts: The accused testified in a civil suit and tendered an agreement that the trial court considered forged.
Before the suit was disposed of, the plaintiffs sought prosecution for false evidence and fabrication of evidence.
When disposing of the suit, the trial court did not record the required opinion and reasons for prosecuting the witness under the special procedure.
The trial court later considered the application after the suit had been disposed of.
issues.conclusion: The trial court could not, after disposing of the suit, make a complaint under the special procedure for intentionally giving false evidence or fabricating evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 479A(1) and 479A(6) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, the special procedure applies to a witness’s intentional giving of false evidence or intentional fabrication of evidence for use in a judicial proceeding. The court must record the required finding and reasons at the time of its judgment or final order; where it has not done so, it cannot make the special-procedure complaint after disposition.

rule.if: judicial_proceeding and witness_false_evidence_or_fabrication_charge and complaint_sought_after_final_disposition and final_order_lacked_required_finding

predicates.judicial_proceeding: The matter was a judicial proceeding in which a person appeared as a witness.
predicates.witness_false_evidence_or_fabrication_ch: The proposed prosecution concerned the witness’s alleged intentional false evidence or fabrication of evidence for use in the proceeding.
predicates.complaint_sought_after_final_disposition: The court was asked to make the complaint after it had finally disposed of the proceeding.
predicates.final_order_lacked_required_finding: The court’s final order did not record the required finding and reasons for prosecuting the witness.

issues.definition: If a witness is sought to be prosecuted for intentional false evidence or fabrication in a judicial proceeding, the request is made after final disposition, and the final order omitted the required finding, the special-procedure complaint is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: The special procedure for false evidence and fabrication does not exclude the court’s general complaint procedure for the distinct offence of fraudulently or dishonestly using a forged document as genuine.
material_facts: The accused testified in a civil suit and tendered an agreement that the trial court found was not genuine.
The trial court did not record the finding required for a special-procedure complaint for false evidence or fabrication when it disposed of the suit.
The trial court directed a complaint under the general procedure for using the agreement as genuine while knowing or having reason to believe it was forged.
The complaint for the use of the document was upheld by the appellate and revisional courts.
issues.conclusion: The offence of using a forged document as genuine did not fall within the special procedure, so the court’s authority to make a complaint under the general procedure was not excluded.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 476 and 479A(1), (6) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, read with section 195(1)(b) and (c), distinguish the general complaint procedure for offences affecting the administration of justice from the special procedure for a witness’s intentional false evidence or fabrication. The offence under section 471 of the Indian Penal Code is not within the category covered by section 479A(1); forgery and fabrication of false evidence are distinct offences, and use of a forged document as genuine is not covered by that special procedure. The Court relied on Raghubir Prasad Dudhwalla v. Chamanlal Mehra and Shabir Hussain Bholu v. State of Maharashtra, explaining that the latter’s reference to section 471 did not alter the limited scope of the special procedure. Accordingly, the general procedure under section 476 remained available.

predicates.court_considers_complaint_for_offense_re: A court considered making a complaint about an offence connected with a judicial proceeding.
predicates.accused_used_document_as_genuine: The accused presented or used a document as genuine.
predicates.accused_knew_or_believed_document_was_fo: The accused knew or had reason to believe that the document was forged.
predicates.charged_conduct_was_document_use_not_fal: The conduct charged was using the document as genuine, rather than giving false testimony or fabricating evidence.

issues.definition: When a court considers a complaint about an offence connected with a judicial proceeding and the accused knowingly or believingly used a forged document as genuine, the general complaint procedure remains available if the charged conduct is document use rather than false testimony or fabrication.
